attacker_pocs.name: ntfs-tag1-oversize-copy
attacker_pocs.why: A stored ZIP entry whose 0x000A NTFS extra field contains tag 0x0001 with a declared attribute length of 64, all of which fits inside the extra field. process_extra accepts that length against the field end, then memcpy's the whole attribute into a 24-byte FILETIME temporary.

role_a_rationale: The ZIP reader now parses extra field 0x000A: after the 4-byte reserved prefix it walks tag/size attributes, converts tag 0x0001's mtime/atime/creation FILETIMEs with __archive_ntfs_to_unix, publishes creation as birthtime only when that tag is present, and keeps sub-second nsec unless a later 1-second source (DOS, UT, UX, PKWARE Unix) overwrites the seconds. Attribute lengths are rejected when they run past the extra field, so a short or truncated field does not fault and leaves birthtime unset. The new path copies a tag-0x0001 attribute with memcpy(ft, ..., sz) into uint64_t ft[3]. The minimum-size test is sz >= 24 and the source is limited to the extra field, but the copy length is the full attribute size, so a longer in-spec attribute (padding past the three FILETIMEs) overflows that stack buffer. A standard 24-byte tag does not. The same bytes are ignored on the parent, which has no 0x000A case.
